# variplex

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://img.shields.io/cran/v/variplex)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=variplex)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/rheradio/variplex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rheradio/variplex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

variplex computes, for a variability model, every relationship between two features that holds in all its valid
configurations, and analyses the resulting graphs from R:

- **requires**: every valid configuration with A also has B;
- **excludes**: no valid configuration has both A and B;
- **at least one**: no valid configuration lacks both.

The model can be a feature model in [UVL](https://universal-variability-language.github.io/), or the Boolean formula
(DIMACS) of a model written in any other notation, such as the Kconfig files of the Linux kernel translated by KMax,
KConfigReader or KconfigSampler. A SAT solver finds the relationships once; then more than a hundred functions answer
questions about them without a solver, and return tibbles: what each feature weighs, how the model is layered, where
its conflicts come from, which features can go together, how much of the model a test sample covers, which patterns
recur, and how the model changes from version to version.

variplex brings together the engine of [Strong4VM](https://github.com/rheradio/strong4vm) (C++, compiled into the
package with the SAT solver Glucose) and its R functions, which were named `sg_*` and are now `vp_*`.

## Installation

```r
install.packages("variplex")
```

Nothing has to be installed outside R. To draw the graphs, install also the suggested packages DiagrammeR (and
DiagrammeRsvg and rsvg to save drawings as SVG, PDF or PNG). The development version is on GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rheradio/variplex")
```

## Example

```{r example}
library(variplex)

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3_realized.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
band

vp_requirements(band, "TouchScreen") # what the touch screen brings along
# why two features never go together
vp_explain_conflict(band, "MovementFilter", "BT40")
vp_can_go_together(
  band,
  list(c("TouchScreen", "HeartRateSensor"), c("TouchScreen", "BT40"))
)
```

```r
vp_plot(vp_minimal(band))                          # with DiagrammeR
```

## From the command line of Strong4VM to R

| `strong4vm` | variplex |
|:--|:--|
| `strong4vm model.uvl -o out --or-graph --kernel` | `vp_generate("model.uvl", output_dir = "out", or_graph = TRUE, kernel = TRUE)` |
| `strong4vm formula.dimacs --classify-only` | `vp_classify("formula.dimacs")` |
| `strong4vm check out/model` | `vp_check(vp_read("out/model"))` |
| `strong4vm expand out/model` | `vp_expand(vp_read("out/model", form = "minimal"))` |
| `strong4vm explain out/model --conflict A B` | `vp_explain_conflict(model, "A", "B")` |
| `strong4vm explain out/model --requires A B` | `vp_explain_requires(model, "A", "B")` |
| `strong4vm diff old new` | `vp_compare(old, new)`, `vp_changed_links(old, new)`, `vp_state_moves(old, new)` |
| `strong4vm diff --rename FILE old new` | `vp_compare(vp_rename(old, FILE), new)` |

Every option of `strong4vm generate` is an argument of `vp_generate()`; `?vp_generate` lists them.

## Documentation

Start with `vignette("variplex")`. The other vignettes go through the results (`vignette("graphs")`) and every
question the graphs answer, topic by topic; `vp_functions()` lists the functions by topic.

## What the graphs cannot see

The graphs hold relationships between **two** features. A rule that ties three or more features at once ("A requires B
or C") is in no graph, unless it implies a relationship between two of them. Everything the graphs say is true; a
"yes" to a long wish list can still be wrong. `vignette("limits-theory")` explains it, measures it and proves it.

## Citation

`citation("variplex")`. The dataset of graphs of 5,709 variability models made with Strong4VM is at
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17277788>.
